description: Comprehensive question bank on Rocks (Physical Geography) derived from the provided study notes. Verify before formal examination use.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What is a rock?

options.A: A naturally occurring solid aggregate of one or more minerals, mineraloids, or organic materials forming part of the Earth's crust
options.B: A liquid substance found only in the Earth's core
options.C: A synthetic material made by humans
options.D: A type of fossil fuel only

questions.explanation: A rock is a naturally occurring solid aggregate of one or more minerals, mineraloids, or organic materials that forms part of the Earth's crust.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What are rocks the basic solid materials of?

options.A: The atmosphere

questions.explanation: Rocks are the basic solid materials of the lithosphere.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What is a mineral?

options.A: A naturally occurring, usually inorganic solid with a definite or limited chemical composition and an ordered internal crystal structure
options.C: A type of rock formed from lava

questions.explanation: A mineral is a naturally occurring, usually inorganic solid with a definite or limited chemical composition and an ordered internal crystal structure.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a mineral?

options.A: Granite

questions.explanation: Quartz is a mineral. Granite, basalt, and obsidian are rocks.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What is the difference between a rock and a mineral?

options.A: A mineral has a characteristic chemical composition and crystal structure; a rock is an aggregate or mass that may contain one or several minerals
options.B: A rock is always larger than a mineral
options.C: A mineral is always organic; a rock is always inorganic

questions.explanation: A mineral has a characteristic chemical composition and crystal structure; a rock is an aggregate or mass that may contain one or several minerals.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: Granite commonly contains which of the following minerals?

options.A: Quartz, feldspar and mica

questions.explanation: Granite commonly contains quartz, feldspar and mica.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: Are all rocks made of minerals?

options.A: Yes, all rocks are made entirely of minerals
options.B: No, some rocks contain mineraloids or organic material
options.D: No, rocks are made only of organic material

questions.explanation: No. Some rocks contain mineraloids or organic material. Coal is largely derived from accumulated plant matter, while volcanic glass such as obsidian lacks an orderly crystalline structure.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: Coal is largely derived from which material?

options.A: Accumulated plant matter

questions.explanation: Coal is largely derived from accumulated plant matter.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: Which volcanic glass lacks an orderly crystalline structure?

options.A: Granite

questions.explanation: Volcanic glass such as obsidian lacks an orderly crystalline structure.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What is petrology?

options.A: The branch of geology that studies the origin, composition, structure, classification and transformation of rocks

questions.explanation: Petrology is the branch of geology that studies the origin, composition, structure, classification and transformation of rocks.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What is lithology?

options.A: The physical characteristics of a rock, including its colour, grain size, texture and mineral composition
options.B: The study of the Earth's atmosphere
options.D: The chemical analysis of minerals only

questions.explanation: Lithology refers to the physical characteristics of a rock, including its colour, grain size, texture and mineral composition.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: How are rocks mainly classified?

options.A: Into three major groups according to their origin and mode of formation: igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic

questions.explanation: Rocks are classified into three major groups according to their origin and mode of formation: igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: How do igneous rocks form?

options.A: By the cooling and solidification of molten magma or lava
options.B: Through the accumulation, deposition, compaction and cementation of sediments
options.C: When pre-existing rocks are changed by heat, pressure and chemically active fluids

questions.explanation: Igneous rocks form by the cooling and solidification of molten magma or lava.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: How do sedimentary rocks form?

options.A: Through the accumulation, deposition, compaction and cementation of sediments, or by chemical/biological precipitation
options.C: By the complete melting of older rocks

questions.explanation: Sedimentary rocks form through the accumulation, deposition, compaction and cementation of sediments, or by chemical/biological precipitation.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: How do metamorphic rocks form?

options.A: When pre-existing rocks are changed by heat, pressure and chemically active fluids without completely melting
options.B: By the cooling of lava on the surface
options.C: By the evaporation of saline water
options.D: By the accumulation of plant remains

questions.explanation: Metamorphic rocks form when pre-existing rocks are changed by heat, pressure and chemically active fluids without completely melting.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: Which rock groups make up most of the crust by volume?

options.A: Igneous and metamorphic rocks

questions.explanation: Igneous and metamorphic rocks make up most of the crust by volume, whereas sedimentary rocks cover a much larger proportion of the exposed land surface.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: Which rock group covers a much larger proportion of the exposed land surface?

options.A: Igneous rocks

questions.explanation: Sedimentary rocks cover a much larger proportion of the exposed land surface.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What is the difference between crustal volume and surface coverage of rock types?

options.A: Igneous and metamorphic rocks dominate by volume, while sedimentary rocks dominate surface coverage
options.B: Sedimentary rocks dominate both volume and surface coverage
options.C: Igneous rocks dominate both volume and surface coverage
options.D: Metamorphic rocks dominate both volume and surface coverage

questions.explanation: Igneous and metamorphic rocks make up most of the crust by volume, whereas sedimentary rocks cover a much larger proportion of the exposed land surface. Do not confuse crustal volume with surface coverage.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What are igneous rocks?

options.A: Rocks formed when molten rock material cools and solidifies
options.C: Rocks formed by heat and pressure without melting

questions.explanation: Igneous rocks are formed when molten rock material cools and solidifies.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What is magma?

options.A: Molten material below the Earth's surface
options.B: Molten material that reaches the surface

questions.explanation: Magma is molten material below the Earth's surface.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What is lava?

options.A: Molten material that reaches the surface
options.B: Molten material below the Earth's surface

questions.explanation: Lava is molten material that reaches the surface.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: Why are igneous rocks called primary rocks?

options.A: Because they form directly from the cooling of magma or lava and can provide the parent material from which sedimentary and metamorphic rocks develop
options.B: Because they are the oldest rocks on Earth
options.C: Because they are found only on the surface
options.D: Because they contain the most fossils

questions.explanation: They are called primary rocks because they form directly from the cooling of magma or lava and can provide the parent material from which sedimentary and metamorphic rocks develop.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What are the main characteristics of igneous rocks?

options.A: Generally hard, compact and crystalline; usually lack fossils; commonly show interlocking mineral grains; generally not arranged in sedimentary layers
options.B: Always soft and porous; contain abundant fossils; arranged in layers

questions.explanation: Igneous rocks are generally hard, compact and crystalline; usually lack fossils; commonly show interlocking mineral grains; and are generally not arranged in sedimentary layers.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What does the texture of igneous rocks depend strongly on?

options.A: Cooling rate

questions.explanation: The texture of igneous rocks depends strongly on cooling rate.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: How does slow cooling affect igneous rock texture?

options.A: It allows crystals to grow large

questions.explanation: Slow cooling allows crystals to grow large.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: How does rapid cooling affect igneous rock texture?

options.A: It produces small crystals

questions.explanation: Rapid cooling produces small crystals.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: How does extremely rapid cooling affect igneous rock texture?

options.A: It may produce volcanic glass with little or no visible crystal structure

questions.explanation: Extremely rapid cooling may produce volcanic glass with little or no visible crystal structure.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: How are igneous rocks classified by place of formation?

options.A: As intrusive (below the surface) and extrusive (at or near the surface)

questions.explanation: They are broadly classified as intrusive (below the surface) and extrusive (at or near the surface). Hypabyssal rocks form at shallow depths and are sometimes treated as a separate subcategory.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What are hypabyssal rocks?

options.A: Rocks that form at shallow depths
options.C: Rocks that form on the surface

questions.explanation: Hypabyssal rocks form at shallow depths and are sometimes treated as a separate subcategory.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What are intrusive igneous rocks?

options.A: Rocks that form when magma cools and solidifies beneath the Earth's surface
options.B: Rocks that form when lava cools on the surface
options.C: Rocks that form from compacted sediments
options.D: Rocks that form from plant remains

questions.explanation: Intrusive or plutonic igneous rocks form when magma cools and solidifies beneath the Earth's surface.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: Why do intrusive igneous rocks generally have large crystals?

options.A: Magma loses heat relatively slowly underground, giving mineral crystals more time to grow
options.B: They cool very rapidly at the surface
options.D: They are formed from compacted sediments

questions.explanation: Magma loses heat relatively slowly underground, giving mineral crystals more time to grow. This commonly produces a coarse-grained texture.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What texture do intrusive igneous rocks commonly have?

options.A: Coarse-grained

questions.explanation: Intrusive igneous rocks commonly have a coarse-grained texture with visible interlocking crystals.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What are the main characteristics of intrusive igneous rocks?

options.A: Commonly coarse-grained, have visible interlocking crystals, and may occur as large underground bodies such as batholiths, stocks, dykes and sills

questions.explanation: Intrusive igneous rocks are commonly coarse-grained, have visible interlocking crystals, and may occur as large underground bodies such as batholiths, stocks, dykes and sills.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What is a batholith?

options.A: A very large intrusive igneous body, generally irregular in shape and exposed over a large area after erosion removes overlying rocks

questions.explanation: A batholith is a very large intrusive igneous body, generally irregular in shape and exposed over a large area after erosion removes overlying rocks.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What is a dyke?

options.A: A sheet-like igneous intrusion that cuts across the pre-existing rock layers or structures
options.B: A sheet-like igneous intrusion that is broadly parallel to the pre-existing rock layers

questions.explanation: A dyke is a sheet-like igneous intrusion that cuts across the pre-existing rock layers or structures.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What is a sill?

options.A: A sheet-like igneous intrusion that is broadly parallel to the pre-existing rock layers
options.B: A sheet-like igneous intrusion that cuts across the pre-existing rock layers

questions.explanation: A sill is a sheet-like igneous intrusion that is broadly parallel to the pre-existing rock layers.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a common example of an intrusive igneous rock?

options.A: Granite

questions.explanation: Granite, diorite and gabbro are common examples of intrusive igneous rocks. Basalt, obsidian and pumice are extrusive.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is an important intrusive ultramafic rock?

options.A: Peridotite

questions.explanation: Peridotite is an important intrusive ultramafic rock.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an intrusive igneous rock?

options.A: Granite

questions.explanation: Basalt is an extrusive igneous rock. Granite, diorite and gabbro are intrusive.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What are extrusive igneous rocks?

options.A: Rocks that form when lava cools and solidifies at or near the Earth's surface
options.B: Rocks that form when magma cools deep underground
options.C: Rocks that form from compacted sediments
options.D: Rocks that form from plant remains

questions.explanation: Extrusive or volcanic igneous rocks form when lava cools and solidifies at or near the Earth's surface.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: Why are extrusive igneous rocks generally fine-grained?

options.A: Lava usually cools much faster at the surface than magma cools underground, so crystals have little time to grow
options.C: They are formed from compacted sediments

questions.explanation: Lava usually cools much faster at the surface than magma cools underground, so crystals have little time to grow.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What are the main characteristics of extrusive igneous rocks?

options.A: Commonly fine-grained or glassy, may contain gas-bubble cavities called vesicles, and can form lava flows, volcanic cones and volcanic plateaus
options.B: Commonly coarse-grained with large visible crystals

questions.explanation: Extrusive igneous rocks are commonly fine-grained or glassy, may contain gas-bubble cavities called vesicles, and can form lava flows, volcanic cones and volcanic plateaus.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What is a vesicular texture?

options.A: A texture containing rounded or elongated cavities left by gas bubbles trapped in cooling lava
options.B: A texture with large visible crystals
options.C: A texture with alternating light and dark bands

questions.explanation: A vesicular texture is a texture containing rounded or elongated cavities left by gas bubbles trapped in cooling lava.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an extrusive igneous rock?

options.A: Basalt

questions.explanation: Basalt, rhyolite, andesite, obsidian, pumice and scoria are examples of extrusive igneous rocks.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: Which is the most common extrusive igneous rock?

options.A: Basalt

questions.explanation: Basalt is the most widespread volcanic rock and forms much of the oceanic crust.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What is the difference between magma and lava?

options.A: Magma is molten rock beneath the Earth's surface; lava is magma that has erupted onto the surface
options.B: Lava is molten rock beneath the Earth's surface; magma is molten rock on the surface
options.C: They are exactly the same thing
options.D: Magma is solid; lava is liquid

questions.explanation: Magma is molten rock beneath the Earth's surface; lava is magma that has erupted onto the surface.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an extrusive igneous rock?

options.A: Rhyolite

questions.explanation: Gabbro is an intrusive igneous rock. Rhyolite, andesite and scoria are extrusive.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: Which extrusive rock is glassy and lacks an orderly crystalline structure?

options.A: Obsidian

questions.explanation: Obsidian is a volcanic glass that lacks an orderly crystalline structure.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What are sedimentary rocks?

options.A: Rocks that form from sediments deposited in layers and later compacted and cemented, or from minerals precipitated from water, or from accumulated biological remains
options.B: Rocks that form from the cooling of magma
options.C: Rocks that form from heat and pressure without melting
options.D: Rocks that form from volcanic glass

questions.explanation: Sedimentary rocks form from sediments deposited in layers and later compacted and cemented, or from minerals precipitated from water, or from accumulated biological remains.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What is the correct sequence of processes in the formation of sedimentary rocks?

options.A: Weathering → erosion and transport → deposition → compaction → cementation

questions.explanation: Weathering breaks down existing rocks; erosion and transport move the material; deposition lays it down; compaction squeezes sediments; and cementation binds grains together. These processes are part of lithification.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What is lithification?

options.A: The conversion of loose sediment into solid sedimentary rock, mainly through compaction and cementation
options.B: The melting of rocks into magma
options.C: The cooling of lava into igneous rock
options.D: The alignment of minerals under pressure

questions.explanation: Lithification is the conversion of loose sediment into solid sedimentary rock, mainly through compaction and cementation.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What is bedding or stratification?

options.A: The arrangement of sedimentary material into layers or strata, often reflecting changes in the conditions of deposition
options.B: The alignment of minerals in metamorphic rocks
options.C: The growth of crystals from magma
options.D: The formation of gas bubbles in lava

questions.explanation: Bedding is the arrangement of sedimentary material into layers or strata, often reflecting changes in the conditions of deposition.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What are the main characteristics of sedimentary rocks?

options.A: Commonly occur in layers, may contain fossils, often have grains or fragments cemented together, and may show ripple marks, mud cracks or cross-bedding

questions.explanation: Sedimentary rocks commonly occur in layers, may contain fossils, often have grains or fragments cemented together, and may show ripple marks, mud cracks or cross-bedding. They are generally more porous than many igneous and metamorphic rocks.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: Why are fossils commonly found in sedimentary rocks?

options.A: Sediments can rapidly bury and preserve remains or traces of organisms
options.B: Sedimentary rocks are formed at very high temperatures
options.C: Sedimentary rocks are always formed from volcanic material

questions.explanation: Sediments can rapidly bury and preserve remains or traces of organisms. The heat and pressure involved in forming many igneous rocks, and in strong metamorphism, usually destroy fossils.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: Why are fossils usually absent from igneous and strongly metamorphosed rocks?

options.A: The heat and pressure involved in their formation usually destroy fossils
options.C: Fossils are only found in volcanic rocks
options.D: Fossils are destroyed by weathering only

questions.explanation: The heat and pressure involved in forming many igneous rocks, and in strong metamorphism, usually destroy fossils.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: Are all sedimentary rocks formed from fragments?

options.A: No. Some form by chemical precipitation, such as rock salt, while others form from biological material, such as many limestones and coal
options.B: Yes, all sedimentary rocks are clastic
options.C: No, all sedimentary rocks are organic
options.D: Yes, all sedimentary rocks are chemical

questions.explanation: No. Some form by chemical precipitation, such as rock salt, while others form from biological material, such as many limestones and coal.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: Where do sedimentary rocks commonly form?

options.A: In rivers, lakes, deserts, deltas, floodplains, beaches, shallow seas and deep ocean basins

questions.explanation: Sedimentary rocks commonly form in rivers, lakes, deserts, deltas, floodplains, beaches, shallow seas and deep ocean basins.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What are mechanical or clastic sedimentary rocks?

options.A: Rocks that form from fragments of pre-existing rocks and minerals that are transported, deposited, compacted and cemented
options.B: Rocks that form from dissolved substances precipitating from water
options.C: Rocks that form from accumulated remains of organisms
options.D: Rocks that form from cooling magma

questions.explanation: Mechanical or clastic sedimentary rocks form from fragments of pre-existing rocks and minerals that are transported, deposited, compacted and cemented.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a mechanical/clastic sedimentary rock?

options.A: Sandstone

questions.explanation: Conglomerate, breccia, sandstone, siltstone and shale are examples of mechanical/clastic sedimentary rocks.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What is the difference between conglomerate and breccia?

options.A: Conglomerate contains mainly rounded rock fragments; breccia contains mainly angular fragments
options.B: Conglomerate contains mainly angular fragments; breccia contains mainly rounded fragments
options.C: Conglomerate is chemical; breccia is organic

questions.explanation: Conglomerate contains mainly rounded rock fragments; breccia contains mainly angular fragments.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What is sandstone?

options.A: A clastic sedimentary rock composed mainly of sand-sized grains, commonly quartz and/or feldspar, held together by natural cement
options.B: A chemical sedimentary rock made of halite
options.C: An organic sedimentary rock made of plant remains
options.D: A metamorphic rock made of recrystallised quartz

questions.explanation: Sandstone is a clastic sedimentary rock composed mainly of sand-sized grains, commonly quartz and/or feldspar, held together by natural cement.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What is shale?

options.A: A fine-grained clastic sedimentary rock formed mainly from compacted clay- and silt-sized particles, commonly splitting along thin bedding planes
options.B: A coarse-grained clastic sedimentary rock made of rounded pebbles
options.C: A chemical sedimentary rock made of halite
options.D: A metamorphic rock with slaty cleavage

questions.explanation: Shale is a fine-grained clastic sedimentary rock formed mainly from compacted clay- and silt-sized particles. It commonly splits along thin bedding planes.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a fine-grained clastic sedimentary rock?

options.A: Shale

questions.explanation: Shale is a fine-grained clastic sedimentary rock formed mainly from compacted clay- and silt-sized particles.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What are chemical sedimentary rocks?

options.A: Rocks that form when dissolved substances precipitate from water, often because of evaporation, changes in temperature or chemistry, or other conditions
options.B: Rocks that form from fragments of pre-existing rocks
options.C: Rocks that form from accumulated remains of organisms
options.D: Rocks that form from cooling magma

questions.explanation: Chemical sedimentary rocks form when dissolved substances precipitate from water, often because of evaporation, changes in temperature or chemistry, or other conditions.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a chemical sedimentary rock?

options.A: Rock salt (halite)

questions.explanation: Rock salt (halite), gypsum and some limestones such as travertine are examples of chemical sedimentary rocks.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: How is rock salt formed?

options.A: It commonly forms when saline water evaporates and dissolved sodium chloride precipitates and accumulates
options.B: It forms from compacted plant remains

questions.explanation: Rock salt commonly forms when saline water evaporates and dissolved sodium chloride precipitates and accumulates.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What is an evaporite?

options.A: A sedimentary deposit formed by precipitation of minerals as water evaporates, commonly including gypsum and halite
options.B: An igneous rock formed from lava
options.C: A metamorphic rock formed under pressure

questions.explanation: An evaporite is a sedimentary deposit formed by precipitation of minerals as water evaporates, commonly including gypsum and halite.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is an evaporite mineral?

options.A: Gypsum

questions.explanation: Evaporites commonly include gypsum and halite.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What are organic or biogenic sedimentary rocks?

options.A: Rocks that form from the accumulated remains or products of organisms, including plant material, shells and microscopic skeletal remains
options.B: Rocks that form from fragments of pre-existing rocks
options.C: Rocks that form from dissolved substances precipitating from water
options.D: Rocks that form from cooling magma

questions.explanation: Organic or biogenic sedimentary rocks form from the accumulated remains or products of organisms, including plant material, shells and microscopic skeletal remains.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is an organic sedimentary rock?

options.A: Coal

questions.explanation: Coal and many limestones, including chalk and coquina, are important examples of organic sedimentary rocks.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: How is coal formed?

options.A: Mainly from accumulated plant remains in waterlogged, oxygen-poor environments; burial, compaction, heat and time progressively convert peat into lignite, bituminous coal and, at higher rank, anthracite
options.B: From the evaporation of saline water

questions.explanation: Coal forms mainly from accumulated plant remains in waterlogged, oxygen-poor environments. Burial, compaction, heat and time progressively convert peat into lignite, bituminous coal and, at higher rank, anthracite.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What is the simplified sequence of coal formation?

options.A: Plant remains → peat → lignite → bituminous coal → anthracite

questions.explanation: A simplified sequence is plant remains → peat → lignite → bituminous coal → anthracite. The sequence represents increasing coal rank, not a process that every deposit follows identically.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What does the coal formation sequence represent?

options.A: Increasing coal rank

questions.explanation: The sequence represents increasing coal rank, not a process that every deposit follows identically.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What is chalk?

options.A: A soft, fine-grained limestone composed largely of microscopic calcareous remains of marine organisms
options.C: A chemical sedimentary rock made of halite
options.D: A metamorphic rock formed from shale

questions.explanation: Chalk is a soft, fine-grained limestone composed largely of microscopic calcareous remains of marine organisms.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a biogenic carbonate rock?

options.A: Coquina

questions.explanation: Coal and many limestones, including chalk and coquina, are important examples of organic sedimentary rocks. Some classification systems distinguish biogenic carbonate rocks from strictly organic-rich rocks.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What are metamorphic rocks?

options.A: Rocks formed when pre-existing igneous, sedimentary or older metamorphic rocks are altered by heat, pressure and chemically active fluids, without undergoing complete melting
options.B: Rocks formed from the cooling of magma

questions.explanation: Metamorphic rocks are formed when pre-existing igneous, sedimentary or older metamorphic rocks are altered by heat, pressure and chemically active fluids, without undergoing complete melting.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What is metamorphism?

options.A: The mineralogical, chemical and textural change of a rock in the solid state in response to changed physical or chemical conditions
options.B: The complete melting of a rock
options.C: The cooling of lava into igneous rock

questions.explanation: Metamorphism is the mineralogical, chemical and textural change of a rock in the solid state in response to changed physical or chemical conditions.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What are the main agents of metamorphism?

options.A: Heat, pressure (including directed stress) and chemically active fluids

questions.explanation: Heat, pressure (including directed stress) and chemically active fluids are the principal agents of metamorphism.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What are the main characteristics of metamorphic rocks?

options.A: May show recrystallised minerals, foliation or banding, increased hardness or density, and new minerals stable under the changed conditions; fossils may be distorted or destroyed

questions.explanation: Metamorphic rocks may show recrystallised minerals, foliation or banding, increased hardness or density, and new minerals stable under the changed conditions. Fossils may be distorted or destroyed.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What is foliation?

options.A: A planar arrangement of minerals or mineral bands produced commonly by directed pressure during metamorphism
options.C: The growth of crystals from magma
options.D: The formation of gas bubbles in lava

questions.explanation: Foliation is a planar arrangement of minerals or mineral bands produced commonly by directed pressure during metamorphism.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: Are all metamorphic rocks foliated?

options.A: No. Some are non-foliated; marble and quartzite are common examples
options.B: Yes, all metamorphic rocks are foliated
options.C: No, all metamorphic rocks are non-foliated

questions.explanation: No. Some are non-foliated. Marble and quartzite are common examples of non-foliated metamorphic rocks.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a non-foliated metamorphic rock?

options.A: Marble

questions.explanation: Marble and quartzite are common examples of non-foliated metamorphic rocks.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What is recrystallisation?

options.A: The growth or rearrangement of mineral crystals in the solid state, commonly producing larger or more stable crystals
options.B: The melting of crystals into magma

questions.explanation: Recrystallisation is the growth or rearrangement of mineral crystals in the solid state, commonly producing larger or more stable crystals.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What is regional metamorphism?

options.A: Metamorphism that affects large areas of the Earth's crust, usually during mountain-building events where rocks experience elevated temperature and directed pressure at depth
options.B: Metamorphism that affects a narrow zone around an igneous intrusion

questions.explanation: Regional metamorphism affects large areas of the Earth's crust, usually during mountain-building events where rocks experience elevated temperature and directed pressure at depth.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: Where does regional metamorphism commonly occur?

options.A: In convergent plate-margin and continental collision settings, especially in deeply buried and deformed mountain belts

questions.explanation: Regional metamorphism commonly occurs in convergent plate-margin and continental collision settings, especially in deeply buried and deformed mountain belts.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: Which rocks can form through regional metamorphism?

options.A: Slate, phyllite, schist, gneiss and regional varieties of quartzite or marble

questions.explanation: Depending on the original rock and metamorphic grade, examples include slate, phyllite, schist, gneiss and regional varieties of quartzite or marble.

questions.subject: Physical Geography
questions.question: What is metamorphic grade?

options.A: A general indication of the intensity of metamorphism, often related to temperature and pressure
options.B: The colour of a metamorphic rock
options.C: The fossil content of a metamorphic rock
